entries.notes: Paper runs aeon's TimeSeriesForestRegressor(n_estimators=500) via a per-channel ensemble wrapper (identity for univariate data); libraryts runs sktime's TimeSeriesForestRegressor with the same 500-tree config. The aeon/sktime implementations share the same design (mean/std/slope interval features, min_interval=3), so only the random interval draws differ; tolerance 25% relative was chosen before running for that stochasticity. The paper's headline tables average 30 resamples; this claim targets fold 0, the default split that libraryts evaluates.
entries.train_command: libraryts train --algorithm TimeSeriesForestRegressor --dataset covid-3month --model-id bench-regression-tsf-covid3month --param n_estimators=500 --param random_state=7 --param min_interval=3 --param n_jobs=1

source.venue: Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 38, 2024 / tsml-eval
source.locator: CNN_rmse.csv, row Covid3Month, fold 0 (default train/test split)

entries.notes: Paper runs aeon's TimeCNNRegressor defaults (n_epochs=2000, batch_size=16, kernel_size=7, avg_pool_size=3, 2 conv layers, sigmoid activations, 'valid' padding); sktime's CNNRegressor shares the architecture and epoch budget but defaults to ReLU hidden activations and 'auto' padding — an implementation gap that, together with single-seed stochastic training, motivates the 40% relative tolerance used for the other deep regressors. The paper's headline tables average 30 resamples; this claim targets fold 0, the default split that libraryts evaluates.
entries.train_command: libraryts train --algorithm CNNRegressor --dataset covid-3month --model-id bench-regression-cnn-covid3month --param avg_pool_size=3 --param batch_size=16 --param kernel_size=7 --param n_conv_layers=2 --param n_epochs=2000 --param random_state=0
